items.note: Decided by the sentence AFTER the blank (two loss sizes under two wind directions). 'inevitable' is the natural guess from sentences 1-2 and the last sentence kills it cleanly. Once the third sentence is read there is no contest; easy for the hard route.

'a vindication' kill ('A find does not confirm the schedule') holds exactly. 'a formality' kill is inferential: the named sentence shows the inspection matters, but does not directly address whether a FIND is routine-for-form's-sake; a student who reads 'formality' as 'routine' will hesitate between B and C. Key still best because 'asked to find cracks already large enough to be found' makes the find expected, not perfunctory.

items.read_aloud_flag: 'mute' is an unusual predicate for a rating; slightly stilted
items.note: 'conservative' is the world-true trap (cycle ratings are widely assumed cautious) and the passage kills it: 5000 rated, exhausted after a few hundred = over-promise. 'mute' killed by 'still holds as a ceiling'. Key is bland but the only survivor. Good item.

'seems ___, but ... eleven kilometers' decides it inside the sentence. 'cumulative' is TRUE in the world (the drift does accumulate) and the explanation's kill ('a day's drift' treats it as daily) is weak reasoning; what actually kills it is the 'but' structure, not the named phrase. Not a threat to the key.

'harmless' tempts because 'the master sequence is built to catch this', but the blank is scoped 'In a single core' and 'every date older than the gap shifts by a year' kills it. 'conspicuous' is the direct opposite; 'impossible' killed by sentence 2.

The twist is 'was, and remains' scoped to the earthquake networks; 'an instrument' is what it became for the researchers, not the networks. Key is the plainest option in the set (see batch-level note).

'fast' kill (same switching speed on any die) is exact. 'elegant'/'versatile' are killed only by absence of support, which the explanation admits ('the passage credits it with neither'); that is legitimate WIC practice but is not a passage sentence ruling them out. Key requires the inference yield -> cost per working chip; the passage never says 'cost'. Acceptable.
Colon after the blank explains it in the same sentence. 'uniform' is the antonym, 'lenient' and 'coarse' have no foothold. Easy.
'did not create ... so much as ___' plus 'spread these genes at a speed' settles it. Key is the most VIVID option in its set (one of ~3 in the batch).
'dismissed as evidence of careless mixing' = recorded as a defect. 'a mystery' killed because analysts HAD an explanation. Easy.

The blank is what CRITICS say, so the author's third sentence ('the spread reports exactly how far the forecast can be trusted') does not rule out that critics call the practice 'misleading' - critics need not agree with the author. Worse, the rebuttal 'But the single number was never the commitment it appeared to be ... conceals that it has done so' reads naturally as a tu quoque answer to a 'misleading' charge as well as to an 'indecisive' one. 'indecisive' fits the 'commitment' framing better and is my pick, but a strong student can defend D. HOLD / revise: make the critics' charge unmistakably about refusing to commit (e.g. add 'hedging' language) or change D.

'___ rather than brute' - 'brute' sits three words after the blank and the only option that opposes brute force is 'structured'. The whole passage is scaffolding; the sentence decides it. Batch labels this hard; on the hard route it is easy. Consider moving 'rather than brute' out of the blank sentence if it is meant to be hard.
'as a faint pattern laid over the ordinary image of the sky' (5+ words after the blank) settles it inside the sentence; retina/light earlier make it redundant. 'smell' is a throwaway. Easy.

'destroyed' kill ('not gone') is exact. 'diverted' kill ('held in the river's own basin, not sent somewhere else') is a distinction a student may not grant - trapping sediment on a reservoir floor is a diversion in ordinary usage. What saves the key is the object: the dam ___ 'the delta's one defense', and 'passed through the gates in controlled releases' makes the defense resumable = suspended. Acceptable.

Within the passage every kill holds: usury 'nowhere mentioned' kills evasion, 'known in advance' kills speculation, priced danger kills formality. WORLD-TRUTH flag: the disguised-lending reading (de Roover) is the MAINSTREAM scholarly view, not a recent fad, and the passage asserts the minority position as fact ('the letters are about roads'). A well-read student will feel B is true; the passage does explicitly deny it, so against-the-passage the key stands. Best of the B-series.

'repairing' and 'extending' kills are exact. 'commemorating' kill is arguable: 'chiselled over the last' shows predecessors erased, but a student can read 'commemorating old ones in the name of whoever happened to rule' as marking the road under the current reign - the explanation must reach for 'as though the newcomer had laid the road himself' to get to appropriation, and that clause supports 'claiming' more than it excludes 'commemorating'. WORLD-TRUTH flag: milestones DO frequently record repair (refecit/restituit formulas); passage pre-empts with 'no resurfacing of that date'. Borderline hold.
'is told it may not' is the decider; 'design' is the critics' view and 'smoothed the joins' kills it; 'habit' killed by the writer asking to be spared. Solid.

items.read_aloud_flag: 'an invention of the schoolroom' is slightly stilted (product/creature would be more natural)
items.note: 'convenience' is the printers' view and is killed twice (longer forms; chosen for derivation). 'concession' killed by 'the printing house gave way'. 'a(n)' is warranted here (invention/accident vowel-initial). Fine.

Here the RECEIVED view (hallmark = consumer protection) is the key and the 'guild weapon' reading is the foil - the reverse of the batch's usual shape, which is good for the cross-item tell. 'advisory' killed by 'could not lawfully be sold without'.
Short passage; 'letters ... ask for particular embellishments by name' decides it. 'compromise' is the only live distractor and the letters kill it. Batch says hard; I say medium.

'imposed' is the Conquest-snapshot view; 'no lords to please' kills it. 'settled over generations' is near-idiomatic and 'over generations' immediately after the blank pushes toward a gradual verb, but 'resisted over generations' is also gradual, so the passage is still needed. Key is the plainest option.

items.read_aloud_flag: 'credit' appears verbatim in the passage ('a small credit') as a DISTRACTOR - a lexical-anchor trap that works against the guesser, fine
items.note: The sentence after the blank ('could not buy a train ticket') hands over the answer. 'comparison' kill is inferential (the passage making the comparison does not show scrip never prevented it), but the train-ticket sentence makes it moot. Easy on the hard route.
All three kills are exact and each cites a different clause (same stone; summary figure vs finished strut; same pose with and without). Key is the most VIVID word in its set. Well built.

items.read_aloud_flag: 'a(n)' printed although no option begins with a vowel - should read 'a'
items.note: 'less a ___ than a procedure' opposing 'usually described as mercy' wants the mercy word. The 'punishment' kill is direction-based (the passage shows it punishing, so 'less a punishment' contradicts) and holds, but a student who reads 'procedure' as 'mere paperwork, not real punishment' can argue A; the explanation's logic is right and I'd keep. Fix the 'a(n)'.

'moved it upward every time' plus 'ask that the maxima be cut' decide it. 'unequal' is the historians' reading and the traders' silence on the floor kills it. 'hidden'/'discretionary' killed by the fixed published schedule. Key is the plainest option.

items.read_aloud_flag: 'a(n)' printed although no option begins with a vowel - should read 'a'
items.note: 'find the place at which to rejoin' is a definition of bookmark; 'preview' is the modern misreading and 'passed over the heading' kills it; 'joke' killed by 'grave chapters as evenly'. Easy.

'undetectable' is the strong trap ('recorded nothing at all ... precisely because they were the worst') and 'Those towns felt the shortage, and their prices rose' kills it exactly - the famine is in the record, softened. Good item.

batch_summary.agreement: 27/27 of my blind answers match the key.

drops_or_holds.WIC7A-11: HOLD - 'misleading' survives: the blank is the critics' charge, and the rebuttal ('the single number ... conceals') answers a misleading charge as readily as an indecisive one.
drops_or_holds.WIC7B-02: BORDERLINE - 'commemorating' kill is inferential; 'repairing' is world-true for milestones. Keep only if the two other graders are clean on it.
drops_or_holds.WIC7A-12: KEEP but relabel easy - 'rather than brute' three words after the blank decides it in-sentence.

batch_summary.difficulty_disagreements: Batch calls A-12 and B-06 hard; I call them easy/medium. Batch calls A-01, A-10, A-13, B-09, B-13 medium; I call them easy. Batch is ~5 items too generous overall for the module-2 hard route.
batch_summary.plainest_vs_vivid: Plainest-word heuristic finds the key in roughly 7/27 (A-06 noise, A-13 see, A-12 structured, A-10 defect, B-08 settled, B-12 rising, B-02 claiming) ~26%, i.e. chance. Most-vivid finds it in ~3/27 (A-09 unleash, B-10 pedigree, B-13 bookmark) ~11%, below chance. Neither register leaks.
batch_summary.received_view_tell: CROSS-ITEM TELL. In 11 of the 12 B-series passages the first sentence states a received view, the passage overturns it, and the option naming the received view is a DISTRACTOR (evasion, repairing, design, convenience, oversight, imposed, credit, workmanship, unequal, preview, undetectable-ish). Only B-05 (protective) and B-11 (reprieve, via 'less a __ than') put the received-view word in the key. A student who learns 'eliminate the option that restates sentence 1' plays at 33% across the B-series without reading past the first sentence. Recommend flipping 2-3 more B-items so the received view is sometimes the key.
batch_summary.world_truth_ruling: Passages assert minority positions as fact in B-01 (bills of exchange were not usury evasion - de Roover's disguised-interest reading is the mainstream), B-02 (milestones never record repair), B-03 (serial cliffhangers were publisher-imposed, not architecture). In each the passage contains an explicit sentence denying the world-true distractor, so against-the-passage the key holds. The exposure is B-01 evasion and B-02 repairing: a strong student who trusts world knowledge over the passage picks them. A-03 conservative and A-04 cumulative are also world-true but killed structurally.
batch_summary.key_slot_spread: Key in slot A on 12/27 (44%); A-series alone 8/14. Must be shuffled before insert; verify-answer-key-spread would flag it.
batch_summary.kill_test_summary: 8 of 27 items have at least one kill that only makes the key more precise rather than ruling the option out (A-02 formality, A-04 cumulative, A-07 elegant/versatile, A-11 misleading, A-14 diverted, B-02 commemorating, B-09 comparison, B-11 punishment). Only A-11 is a real exclusivity failure; the rest are saved by a second sentence or by the sentence frame.
batch_summary.passage_needed_false: A-04, A-08, A-12, A-13 are decided inside the blank sentence (4/27).
